instruction: Make the first textbox bold and red, the second textbox bold and blue, and the third textbox bold and green on slide 1, in top-to-bottom order.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires applying combined formatting (bold+color) to three textboxes on slide 1. Slide 1 has shapes at indices 0, 1, and 4. Expected: all bold with colors red (255,0,0), blue (0,0,255), green (0,255,0). Evaluator provides partial credit for each matching property.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical data type mismatch: Getter returns color as tuple (r, g, b) but expected values are lists [r, g, b], causing color comparisons to always fail
The metric uses strict equality (==) to compare colors, so (255, 0, 0) != [255, 0, 0] will always be False
This will cause the evaluator to return 0.5 score even when colors are correctly applied (only bold checks pass, all color checks fail)
Shape indices [0, 1, 4] correctly target the three textboxes per metadata
Bold comparison logic is correct and will work properly
Postconfig correctly saves file before verification
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Change getter line 40 from 'color = (rgb[0], rgb[1], rgb[2])' to 'color = [rgb[0], rgb[1], rgb[2]]' to return list instead of tuple
Add edge case handling in metric for when color is None (shapes with no runs)
Consider using list(color) or tuple comparison to make metric more robust to type variations
